scenarios.title: Sacrificing is not destruction, so regeneration cannot save the permanent, and only the instructed player's own permanents are sacrificed
decisions: A casts Diabolic Edict targeting B, tapping both Swamps.
A passes priority; B activates Cudgel Troll's regenerate ability, tapping Forest.
Both players pass; the regeneration ability resolves and creates a shield.
Both players pass; Diabolic Edict resolves and B sacrifices a creature.

variants.label: sacrifice
variants.expected: B sacrifices Cudgel Troll, the only creature B controls: it moves directly to B's graveyard despite the regeneration shield. A's Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield, because A is not the player who sacrifices.

variants.label: destroy
variants.delta: A casts Doom Blade targeting Cudgel Troll instead of Diabolic Edict.
variants.expected: The destruction is replaced by the regeneration shield: Cudgel Troll stays on the battlefield, tapped, with damage removed.

variants.label: no_creature
variants.expected: B has nothing to sacrifice. Nothing is sacrificed, and A's Grizzly Bears stays on the battlefield.
